messages.subject: Measurement invariance
parts:
Dear all,

I'm writing a paper and used SEM tot test a model in lavaan. I conducted two multi-group analyses using measurement invariance testing, but i'm a bit stuck for the conclusions of the outcomes. 

- The first multi-group gained me strong invariance, this means I can compare the groups. But can I state that de differences in the regressions are significant? That one effect is significantly higher for the first group f.e.? Or do I need extra analyses to make this conclusion? 

- The second multi-group gave me strict invariance. Can I conclude that both groups are equal? Because I would like to do so. 

Thank you for your time!
Cheers,
Fiona

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Measurement invariance
parts:
On 01/15/2015 10:30 AM, Fiona Vande Velde wrote:
> Dear all,
>
> I'm writing a paper and used SEM tot test a model in lavaan. I conducted
> two multi-group analyses using measurement invariance testing, but i'm a
> bit stuck for the conclusions of the outcomes.
>
> - The first multi-group gained me strong invariance, this means I can
> compare the groups. But can I state that de differences in the
> regressions are significant?

You would need to test a model where you constrain the regressions to be
equal versus a model where you allow them to be free (across groups).

> - The second multi-group gave me strict invariance. Can I conclude that
> both groups are equal?

The measurement instrument behaves equal in both groups. But that does
not imply the groups are equal... (ie they can have different values on
the latent variables).

Yves.
